text: For most families in Pakistan, a house is something you build once in a lifetime. The design still happens on paper, over weeks of revisions with a draftsman, and the plan can come back from the development authority over a single setback.
Naqsha is an agentic home design studio, built on Google Cloud.
It's for families planning a home, and for the architects and builders who work with them.

You start with one message about your plot and your family. A Google ADK agent on Gemini 3.8 Flash replies in about four seconds with the brief, floor by floor, including the water tank, a roof kept ready for solar, and the exact area the local authority lets you build on.
Gemini 3.1 Flash Image then draws four exterior concepts from the same camera, so they're easy to compare. These four took twenty-three seconds, and one tap shows all of them at night.

Pick one, and Gemini 4 Argon starts work as the architect. It lays out every floor, room by room. A rules engine checks the plan against the building bylaws and a set of livability rules: every bedroom has its own way in, the stairs reach the roof, and every drop has a railing. Argon fixes whatever fails. On this run it went from fifteen issues to five, then to none. It then looks at a drawing of its own plan and critiques it the way an architect would.
This prototype uses Lahore's LDA bylaws, and this plan passed all thirty-six checks. The drawing set is ready to print, at one to one hundred.

Argon then writes the house in 3D as code, in twenty-eight sections, from the structure and the facade to the furniture in every room. Your browser assembles it live. Orbit the outside, switch to night, or cut away a floor to look into the furnished rooms. Any view can become a photoreal render in about ten seconds.
You can also walk through it like a game: look around the lounge, jump to the master bedroom, take the stairs, and step out onto the roof.

Anyone can pin a note to the exact spot they mean. Share a link with your client or your family, and they can comment without an account. Here, Ammi asks for a bigger kitchen, and her note shows up for the owner right away.

Choose the notes and press Revise. A second ADK agent, also on Argon, with nine tools, reads each note, edits the plan, and runs every check again. The bedroom window gets wider and the kitchen grows. Extending the porch would break the front setback, so the agent explains that and offers another option.
You can also type a change in plain words. Version five has the bigger kitchen and passes thirty-seven of thirty-seven bylaw checks and ten of ten livability checks.

On Google Cloud, one Cloud Run service hosts the app and streams the agent runs. Firestore stores projects, versions and comments, Cloud Storage keeps the images, Firebase Authentication signs people in, and Gemini runs on Vertex AI. Both agents are built with Google's Agent Development Kit.

Families can see and walk through their home before they build it, and architects and builders start from a design that has already been checked. Because the agents read bylaws as data, adding a new city starts with adding its rules. We're starting in Pakistan, and Naqsha is live today.
